questions.question: Extended ASCII (EASCII) is an 8-bit code. How many characters can it represent?
questions.explanation: Extended ASCII uses 8 bits, so it can represent 2^8 = 256 characters. Standard ASCII is a 7-bit code with 128 characters.

questions.question: In data communication, the number of bits transmitted between source and destination in one second is also called:
questions.explanation: Data transfer rate is the number of bits sent per second and is also called bit rate, measured in bps. Bandwidth is a range of frequencies measured in Hz.

questions.question: In which programming language is the Python language itself written?
questions.explanation: Python is written in C. It was developed by Guido van Rossum in 1989 and first released in 1991.

questions.question: Which disk scheduling algorithm is also known as the Elevator Algorithm?
questions.explanation: SCAN scheduling is also called the Elevator Algorithm. SSTF is Shortest Seek Time First and C-LOOK is Circular-LOOK.

questions.concept: Evaluating a postfix expression with a stack
questions.question: Using a stack, what is the value of the postfix expression 7 8 2 * 4 / + ?
questions.explanation: Operands are pushed; each operator pops two values and pushes the result: 8*2 = 16, 16/4 = 4, then 7+4 = 11.

questions.question: Pegasus spyware, which can stealthily enter a smartphone and access its camera and microphone, was developed by:
questions.explanation: Pegasus was developed by NSO and was discovered in 2019. Kaspersky, McAfee and Bitdefender are antivirus products.

questions.question: Which of the following HTML tags is an unpaired (singleton) tag that has no closing tag?
questions.explanation:

    need closing tags.

questions.question: In a file system, the limitation where data files are not linked or mapped to one another is called:
questions.explanation: Data isolation means data files are not linked or mapped. Redundancy is duplication, inconsistency is the same data differing across files, and dependence is programs depending on file structure.

questions.concept: Turing machine as a writing machine
questions.question: Because it can modify its own input, a Turing machine is also called a:
questions.explanation: A Turing machine can modify its own input, so it is also called a writing machine. It uses an infinite tape with a read/write head.

questions.question: The CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) used in IoT was introduced by:
questions.explanation: CoAP is an application layer, client-server protocol introduced by the IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force). MQTT, not CoAP, was developed by IBM.

questions.question: In C++, what is the main purpose of a namespace?

options.A: To display output on the screen
options.B: To allocate memory at run time

questions.explanation: A namespace provides a way to avoid name collisions. Output is done with cout, and main() is the starting point of execution.

questions.concept: Number of ports per IP address
questions.question: A port number is 16 bits long. How many ports can each host have per IP address?
questions.explanation: Each host can have 65535 ports per IP address because the port number is 16 bits. Ports work at the Transport Layer (layer 4) of the OSI model.

questions.concept: Rootkit, botnet, resident virus and backdoor facts
questions.question: Which of the following statements about malware and intrusion tools are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.A: A rootkit provides administrative access along with stealth capability
options.B: A non-resident virus stays in RAM after it is executed
options.C: A botnet is a network of compromised computers often called zombies
options.D: A backdoor is malware that tracks browsing habits and shows popups

questions.explanation: Rootkits give administrative access and stealth, and botnets are networks of compromised zombie computers. A resident virus (not a non-resident one) stays in RAM, and tracking browsing with popups describes adware, not a backdoor.

questions.question: Which testing type combines a collection of modules and tests them as a group, and is done by testers?
questions.explanation: Integration Testing tests a collection of modules combined as a group and is done by testers. Unit Testing tests an individual module and is done by programmers.

questions.concept: Floor division with negatives and precedence
questions.question: What does the Python statement print(-18 // 5, 4 + 2**5 // 10) display?
questions.explanation: // is floor division, so -18 // 5 rounds down to -4. In 4 + 2**5 // 10, ** is applied first (32), then 32 // 10 = 3, giving 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.question: Unicode was developed by Joe Becker, Lee Collins and Mark Davis, who were employees of:
questions.explanation: Unicode was developed by Xerox employees Joe Becker, Lee Collins and Mark Davis, and is maintained by the Unicode Consortium. The ASCII proposal came from Bob Bemer of IBM and was submitted to ANSI.

questions.question: Selection sort (ascending) is applied to the list [8, 7, 13, 1, -9, 4]. What is the list after the first pass?
questions.explanation: In each pass, selection sort picks the smallest element of the unsorted part and swaps it to the front. The smallest value -9 is swapped with 8, giving [-9, 7, 13, 1, 8, 4].

questions.question: When a running process is interrupted, which process state transition takes place?
questions.explanation: An interrupt moves a process from Running back to Ready. Running to Wait/Block happens on an I/O or event wait, and Running to Terminated happens on exit.

questions.question: When a Turing machine is formally defined as an n-tuple, what is the value of n as given in the syllabus?
questions.explanation: The syllabus defines a Turing machine as a 7-tuple, with finite sets of states, input symbols and tape symbols among its components.

questions.question: In which year was the first version of HTML, HTML 1.0, released?
questions.explanation: The first version, HTML 1.0, came in 1993, and HTML was founded by Tim Berners-Lee. 2014 is the year of HTML 5, the latest version.

questions.concept: Range of a Campus Area Network
questions.question: A Campus Area Network (CAN), a group of interconnected LANs, typically covers what range?
questions.explanation: A CAN (Campus or Corporate Area Network) is a group of interconnected LANs with a range of 1 to 5 km. About 10 metres is the range of a PAN.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sensor in IoT?
questions.explanation: An LED is an output device (actuator), not a sensor. BMP280, DHT11 and the photoresistor are sensors.

questions.concept: Clause following WHERE in SQL query order
questions.question: In the SQL query order, which clause comes immediately after the WHERE clause?
questions.explanation: The SQL query order is SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY. HAVING comes after GROUP BY because it applies conditions on aggregate fields.

questions.question: In software engineering, a software patch is best described as:

options.A: A complete rewrite of the system
options.D: A metric used to estimate software size

questions.explanation: A software patch is an emergency fix or a required/critical fix. Requirements are documented in the SRS, and Function Points estimate software size.

questions.question: Which of the five C++ storage specifiers allows an object to be changed after it is created?
questions.explanation: A mutable object can be changed after it is created. Register allocates memory in a register, Automatic is the default for local variables and Static is initialised only once.
